X Rebirth was supposed to be the title that brought the space sim back into the mainstream. Billed as a better easier to pick up and play title with greater RPG elements to grab hold of a new audience.  Instead we got something that most likely will push space sims further towards the abyss.
Don't get me wrong, there is a huge amount of bad press about the game and I disagree with most of the hate, I expected it to be something different especially as it is titled "rebirth". I expected (because I actually paid attention to the vids) to be flying just the one ship, I also expected the cockpit to take up a good portion of the screen. All this I was reasonably happy with.
I do however agree with a lot of those slamming this game for being an "Expensive beta in disguise" except its not even. Despite it supposedly being a full release AAA title it has many game breaking bugs (although the new auto save feature helps dim the pain considerably (yep there was no in game auto-save until recently)), and other bugs that mean you cant really trade etc (that would be one of the main features of the game too, you know TRADE, fight, Build think) However... The Devs seem to be working hard to fix the issues, though if they had've been honest and said it was in alpha or at least beta it would have been much better. I will say this, I have played and recommended games in Alpha that are WAY more polished than this. I could really spend a lot of time picking holes in this but; to be honest I want to love this game for what it could be, rather than what it is.

Bioshock is a First Person Shooter set in the 1960's in a fictional underwater City called Rapture, you play as Jack, a plane crash survivor who ends up outside a mysterious Lighthouse, throughout the game you find yourself facing off against various different enemies like the Splicers who are mutated Humanoids addicted to ADAM and Big Daddies, who's purpose is the protect the Little Sisters.
Throughout Bioshock you are given various tasks by Atlas (Greg Baldwin) and are forced to locate Andre Ryan (Armin Shimerman), your main uses of combat are various Guns and Plasmids (Essentially Magic Powers) which require EVE to use.
Later in the game you are tasked with deciding the fate of the Little Sisters by either Harvesting them or Saving them, Harvesting them nets you the highest possible ADAM, but Saving Them grants you with exclusive benefits that can only be obtained by saving 3 Little Sisters, every 3 Little Sisters gains you a reward and a bonus 200 ADAM, Harvesting Little Sisters grants you 160 ADAM and Saving Them grants you 80 ADAM.
The Little Sister are protected by Big Daddies, Big Daddies are re-purposed Rapture Construction Workers tasked with protecting the Little Sisters while they wander around gathering ADAM from dead Corpses, Big Daddies come with various weapons like the Rivet Gun, heavy drill, rocket launcher, or ion laser, Big Daddies are Neutral and only attack if provoked, either accidentally or on purpose, if you get too close to a Little Sister they will assume an aggressive stance in attempt to scare off the the player, Big Daddies have 3 lights to alert the player of their current mood stance, Yellow is Neutral, Red is Aggressive and Green is Hypnotised.
Bioshock Remastered isn't by any means a "Perfect" port, nor is it a terrible one, as of the writing of this review, it is missing a few essential PC options which Blind Squirrel have stated that there is a patch "On the way".
In my experience I only noticed One texture bug and One crash in the 3 Hours that I played, the mouse was fine, could be better, the FPS was brilliant with no FPS drops.
In conclusion: Bioshock Remastered is less of a Remaster and more of a HD Edition, not enough has been done to it to really call it a Remaster, however it is still worth the £13.99 asking price, Bioshock is truly a great game and is worth playing if you're new to the Franchise.
This review is based upon a free copy of Bioshock Remastered so naturally I couldn't hate on the Remaster, if you haven't bought the game yet, I would personally wait for a few patches to flesh out some bugs before purchasing Bioshock Remastered.

An absolutely amazing game and a well done sequel to Blood Money. The people at IO Interactive decided to raise the stakes by making Agent 47 fight the Agency itself. As usual, the levels are varied and they were all meticulously designed. 47 traverses through various locales and all this is presented to us beautifully. I remember Blood Money being a beautiful game but Absolution upped all this - this game certainly stands out in its genre.
I expected this considering the companies behind the game. After all, high production value can easily yield the necessary results. However, it is not enough to make a game with an interesting story or gameplay and this is where Absolution excels.
For those of you who are new to the franchise: in Hitman you control an assassin whose job - on each level - is to eliminate someone. Stealth should be the preference as while running and gunning is also an option (but makes the game significantly more difficult) picking the silent run method gives a much higher satisfaction. Enemies' clothing can be picked up and disguise is important to get through various parts of each level.
A change to previous installments is that some sequences are specifically action oriented or more linear. Yet, core and hardcore elements are still there. Also, predicting the routes enemies do can be done with the introduction of the so-called "Instinct Mode". I would say that this Hitman is easier on a normal difficulty than its predecessors but one can always go for the additional challenge by picking another difficulty.
All in all, an excellent follow-up to the franchise and, therefore, highly recommended to the fans as well as to the newcomers.

**SPOILER FREE REVIEW**
I was a massive fan of the XIII series and played through them all on the PS3. Now with the PC port here and nearly 300 hours of experience (on the PS3) I can write with some leverage to you.
Graphically, this game is pretty fantastic. Minus some pixelly textures on the sides of the environment, the backgrounds and everything else, spell visuals, weapon details and model textures are pretty high quality, very excellent in terms of a port that was released all the way back in 2010. If you're a fan of CGI, then FFXIII nails this part perfectly. It's pretty tough to judge the quality of this game's CGI when it pretty much looks like something out of real life.
However, for the PC port of this game, this is where FFXIII falls apart here. There are MASSIVE issues with the port regarding FPS. It is very tough to get constant 60FPS everywhere, and for some this will be a massive downside, this was the case for me. Below this review, there are some performance tips that will make or break the game's performance for you. Try these out and see if your PC can achieve 60FPS for this game.
During battles, the game dips to as low as 10FPS when switching paradigms, a form of switching classes mid battle to put it short-like. Aside from FPS issues, FFXIII offers a very indepth battle system that can get very intense against some of the toughest enemies this game as to offer.
Gameplay wise, ignoring all the technical difficulties, the game starts off by holding your hand and explaining what each option does for quite a bit, all the way up to Chapter 5 roughly. The pathways are often just a single path towards your goal, up until Chapter 11 when you reach the open world part. The Paradigm system is underestimated by a lot of people  - not many people choose to manually select their Abilities and just go for Auto Battle. My tip is to change the Default Command to Abilities instead of Auto Battle in the ingame settings menu.
FInal Fantasy XIII is a beautiful game is that often underestimated by a massive majority of the public. If you appreciate visuals, a good JRPG, some bland humour (mostly Sazh's script) and of course, want to give yourself the chance to have a challenge, then I highly recommend this game to you.
**PERFORMANCE TIPS**
- People have been using a program called GeDoSaTo edit the ingame's graphical capabilties, lowering or increasing the resolution beyond 1080p, etc. (Google GeDoSaTo, find a link from github.
- To achieve 60fps in the field, turning off the minimap can be a massive help. For me, I went from around 30FPS fluctuating to 60FPS constantly.
- Unconfirmed FPS fix for everyone but for me, restarting before playing the game gives you a perfect 60FPS performance everywhere, minus some very little stuttering. My build if anyone is wondering...
- GPU: AMD R9 380
- CPU: i5 3470k
- RAM: Corsair Vengeance 8GB.

4X and RTS gaming at its finest [so far], Rebellion is the current apex of the Sins series and it will be very difficult for any other game developer to top this stroke of genius created by Stardock. And having played through EVERY SINGLE Sins installment so far, I feel confident in this list of pros and cons:
PROS:
-Enhanced Graphics vs. Original Sins.
-Despite the graphics boost the game is still older PC friendly.
-A VERY immersive gameplay, AIs even at their easiest difficulty in this game keep you on your toes at all times.
-As stated above, very advanced AI.
-Titan class vessels are able to single handedly turn the tide in battles, or sweep the battle entirely on its own in the right hands.
-Obviously still carries the soul of the original Sins, and in addition feels more encompassing than any of its predecessors.
-With the addition of factions, the number of playable 'races' has been doubled vs. predecessors, again adding to immersiveness and also challenges players will face.
-Strategists will most certainly have a great time playing this game, but it is built so even the newest or novice of strategists can pick up and play without much issue.
-Scale is almost entirely unmatched [Save for games such as X3 Terran Conflict]
-Arrangement of orbital structures is entirely up to the player, giving nearly limitless customization in that area [Save for room, capacity, and grav wells]
-ANYTHING adds a new dynamic to approaching an 'objective' in game. [Pirate raids, other factions attacking, etc.]
-Some very stunning feats can be performed in AT LEAST single player mode. [I for one held down a near-max size, high level ADVENT capital fleet with a max level Vasari Loyalist Titan, and on top of that kept it afloat for my own high level capital fleet to assist. All of my capitals survived save for one I believe, as for the advent, not nearly as well. This required several 'pause' situations however, so this would have been nearly impossible in a multiplayer game.]
-Uncommon strategies, AKA those that the AI are NEVER seen utilizing, can not only throw off AI players but also hamper with human players, adding to gaming experience.
CONS:
-Some methods players can take in gameplay can take AGES even with all game settings set to 'faster' where applicable and with quick start active in the beginning. [It takes me several hours before I start actually attacking other major factions in the game. Days pass before I attain total victory]
+ COUNTER PRO: Game allows you to actually SAVE multiplayer games and continue them for this reason. [Though all players involved need to have the specific game saved, and preferrably AVOID saving to the cloud.]
-As of Rebellion, most AI player full scale assaults late-game [and possibly player led assaults should they do the same, WITH their titan I might add] will almost certainly wipe out any one planet they are thrown at. [Even with full research, max tactical capacity, TWO starbases, repair stations AND full blown minefield, this is a tall order for said defenses. unless you have a sizeable fleet to counter, or your own titan present, you might as well kiss it all on that planet goodbye.]
-Even with SIX factions now available, there are still only three races [A problem that Supreme Commander shared three years prior to the release of Sins of a Solar Empire]
+ COUNTER PRO: With each faction having a unique titan and several unique research items, the above con is slightly nullified, but it still remains.
-Some graphics seem to sputter when loading a save game. [The surface texture of stars turns into a sort of pixel-like shade warping instead of a firey texture being flexed, warped, contracted and expanded.] Though this is almost totally harmless to gaming experience.
SUGGESTIONS FOR NEXT RELEASE:
-A fourth race. [I am anticipating that Stardock will be adding the Vasari's "Unseen Enemy" as either a playable race or as an AI controlled race like the Pirates, though doing the former would add SO MUCH more to the game. I've pictured what their ships look like a multitude of times, and they always come out eerie.]
-SOME Additional balancing for defenses [Beef up some aspects a bit, or add reasearch for late tiers that makes such defenses considerably more self-sustainable against armadas.]
-Expedit gameplay time [Increase research, development, and construction rates (At least for some structures & ships) overall. Decrease ability cooldowns, research, construction and development costs overall (Again, at least for some elements). By any amount in general would add to the replayability of the game.]
-A little bit of fleet balancing. [Why the vasari are missing an anti-structure cruiser is beyond me. Even with their titans, they still have a leg behind (Especially the rebels since their titan packs a smaller punch than that of the loyalist titan) against the Advent and TEC, despite possessing mobile starbases. However the Siege nanites from the Vasari's new capital ship in Rebellion do somewhat fit this role, although not extremely well like the specialized cruisers for the TEC and Advent.]
Overall the game still is a home run, if i were to give it a score between 1 and 100, it would be a 96-97. If you enjoy RTS games, or want an 'excuse' to like them, this is the game for you.

In my opinion, AC4 was the last good AC game to come out. AC1 created the genre, AC2 and its "expansions" expanded it, AC3 fukked a bit here and there, but AC4 took it to the next level.

Overall I really enjoy playing this game. The characters are unique and interesting, and so are the mechanics, such as wavedashing which play a big role in the gameplay. The stages also are interesting as some can change character properities and and hazards to the stages, and also come in a wide variety of flat, non-hazardous stages (which Smash Bros. really needs).
A feature I really like too is the ability to create your own custom skin for each character. This really helps you feel more involved in the character and the game, and the fact that you can use it in non-ranked online matches is even better.
It's a great, hectic, Melee-inspired game which is a lot of fun when playing with a group of your friends.
However I do find playing online with random people not fun due to people abusing quick, strong moves to get quick kills. I understand that some people believe that if it works then why stop doing it, but it's not fun for newcomers to the game. This is more of a gripe on the community more than the game itself though, other than there some moves that need to be slowed down or nerfed in power.
I also feel that this game could have a better ranked online. I feel like the ranked online is basically the exact same as the exhibition matches except you get a small amount of points after each set. I think this could be further expanded upon.
I would also say that some extra content like an adventure mode, challenge packs, or achievements would be good but I am aware that this is currently in developement.
In the end, I still recommend it for playing with friends, and I understand that the game is still in Early Access and under construction. I look forward to seeing what content is to come.
Pros:
+ Unique and interesting characters
+ Fun stages
+ Wide variety of non-hazardous stages
+ Custom skins
+ Interesting mechanics (e.g. wavedashing)
+ Great game for fans of Super Smash Bros.
Cons:
- Some moves are overpowered (imo)
- Online Ranked match can still be further expanded upon
Con but is currently being worked on:
~ More content such as adventure mode, challenges or achievements (am aware this is currently in developement)

You help other people because that's all that's left in the world.

NPCs don't travel out of their system so there is no trade between jumpgates, there is no way to change which faction controls a zone of space, you could have all friendly stations there and the police force will still be of a faction you are at war with possibly, medium trade and fighters exist along with the shipyards for them but there is no way to buy sell or repair them (there is a way to get them but only through getting the pilot to bail in an existing one and claiming it by having a pilot in your crew), hiring a crew is annoying as hell since the only way to see their stats is to hire and assign them or play a stupid smalltalk minigame that isnt even useful (Tracking down the crew in the first place should count as the minigame and their stats should just be visible if you are allied with their faction), Boarding capitals is broken...unless you try to board a capital ship that already has constructor drones. Overall this is a game that has a lot of potential, should it have been released in the state it is and been marketed as a completed game at full price? No. However this game will evolve quickly with the mod and dev support it has and I do not regret spending my money on this game.

Summary: A visually appealing fps with some interesting mechanics, an interesting setting, and a well made max difficulty system.
Visual Appeal: Looks fantastic, even years later.
Sound: You will have to adjust volume settings to hear some of the dialogue over music/vehicles/explosions. Reasonable gun-sound. Vegitation makes some sound when you move through it.
Controls: Fully customizable.
Game-Feel: Mostly good times, except when jumping in max strength mode.
Difficulty: On Delta, the game is at its best. Hard enough to require restarts to checkpoints fairly often, but only because the AI is pretty damn smart. Nothing feels too unfair, for the most part.
Story: Kinda throws you into it and cuts you out of it really fast, but all the meat in the middle is pretty interesting.
Pace: Will probably take you about 12 hours to beat it on Delta difficulty. More if you take the scenic routes.
Atmosphere: A combination of high quality visuals, good lighting, and reasonably decent sound design can lend to some great moments.
Features: Multiplayer no longer supported through GameSpy, but there is multiplayer through Crysis Wars

I jumped on board the Civilization train when Civ2 came out. Since then, I have been a dedicated fan on the series, and in fact all of firaxis' works since then. I even played that facebook civ, which was surprisingly good (except for the constant puzzles). Yet.. this is the first civilization game for which I have felt compelled to leave a review..
As much as it pains me to say, this Civ release does not merit a full title price tag. In terms of gameplay, Civ:Beyond Earth does in fact feel like a glorified mod of Civ5, and not the best one either. The new sci-fi graphics and sound are very nice and well done. Graphically, the game looks much better than civ 5, even though this may not be apparent in screenshots.. however this is not enough to cover up the fact that the core game underneath it all is quite boring.
Though the affinity and starting condition customizations seem like a huge step forward for the franchise, they actually take away all sense of identity for individual players. The AI civs have been axed even further due to the fact that they have a lot less dialogue and options of interaction. The lack of technological ages and culturally themed buildings also detract from the sense of character that the game has. The overall result of the gameplay changes in Civ Beyond Earth make the game feel like a mad dash towards a specific goal. This is very different from the epic, multi-staged journey that civ fans expect. I found it very hard to become attached to my civ, or to care much about winning, as the game quickly becomes a "assign production and trade routes, end turn and repeat cycle." The devs on this game admit to being fans of Endless Space, and the game actually suffers from the same major flaw.. of being extremely well polished, functional, and pretty, but utterly devoid of character.
The flow of the game feels very bland, especially in comparison to the brave new world expansion for civ 5. Being on an alien world provides the game developers with a virtually unlimited number of interesting scenarios to throw at the player, thanks to decades of accumulated fiction that can be drawn upon. Instead, the game presents all of that intrigue in the form of a box of flavor text each time you build a new type of building.
Among some other missed opportunities that are uniquely available to the setting of beyond earth which were missed are.. Under-water or subterranean settlement, more robust and fleshed out space units, natural wonders and catastrophes, sci-fi themed luxury resources.
All in all, this game was a letdown, and quite overrated. Lets hope Civ6 brings a more memorable experience to the table.
EDIT: The AI's aggression needs to be fixed. They are far too passive. I have played 3 games and the only war I have been a part of thus far was one of my own making.
EDIT2: The game lacks a victory summary.. of any kind. What is up with that?? Seriously.

Last Remnant is a very complex and interesting game with lots of unique mechanics. The problem is that the game doesn't really tell you what those mechanics are or how they work. As a result, a lot of things will just seem random or abritrary unless you look things up in the wiki.
If you do spend time on the Wiki, you can find out how arcana magic works, how people skill up, how to level your characters so that they change into certain classes, how to make sure your members learn special abilities and how to manipulate union formations to give the biggest bonus stats. It's also very easy to skip quests and therefore miss important items or recruitable players without using the wiki as many quests become unavailable after certain story developments in the game. However, personally, I found it extremely rewarding to figure out everything and create the optimum setup for my team. It really depends on if you want to invest the time and effort.
The start of the game is pretty slow, as combat is very repetitive until you unlock more skill types to give you a variety of battle options. Contrary to what a lot of people seem to say, you don't have to grind whatsoever. You have the ability to slow time, making it rather easy to avoid the monsters on the field, and as monsters scale with your level you only make the game more difficult if you grind. The reason people think you need to grind is because some of the bosses are very hard, but you're supposed to change your union formations to suit the fight.
The music is very atmospheric, particularly the battle music, though it can sometimes be a tiny bit repetitive if you play for long periods of time. The voice acting is very good and it adds a lot in the battle when the characters yell things out while they fight, but you probably want to keep it in Japanese with subtitles. The English ones aren't that bad, just a bit cheesy.
The game is quite old but some of the graphics are still amazing to me. Everything is really detailed and has it's own atmosphere. Melphina is probably still one of my favorite cities in any game - just stand on the deck and stare out at the waterfalls. It also makes battles a lot cooler, when you're fighting huge dragons and they all look gorgeous. It was very forward for it's time, and even now a lot of games don't do it as well.
As it's a console port, using a controller is much more smooth, and it's easier to hit the buttons during fast-paced quicktime scenes in battles using one. And, as most people didn't seem to know, you can skip cutscenes by hitting Pause/Break (where the scroll lock and print screen buttons are) and then hitting S (Not sure if there are specific controller buttons for this).
Just get it. Seriously. Unless your not intelligent enough to grasp something new like my dad.

The Last Remnant is a unique title.  It manages to have some of the greatest voices on the face of the planet and still manages to fall short due to its writing.  The main character is voiced by Johnny Yong Bosch, so you'd think he'd be able to save the performance, right?  Nope, the writing's that dry and cliched...though moreso the former than the latter.
What does make this game worth recommending, however, is the gameplay.  When I say that the title is unique, I don't mean because of the writing; games have had great voices and bad writing before.  What makes this game unique is that it has a style of gameplay unseen since Chaos World back on the NES.  Rather than controlling one character at a time and fighting monsters that way, you take several characters into a fight and control them as squads.  This isn't a Turn-Based game, either, though it may look it...or not.  This game is the type of thing that is hard to decipher from videos alone, but its more of a Tactical Turn-Based RPG, though I wouldn't go as far as to call it a Strategy RPG.
This game also lends itself to an OK story, but there's enough here to keep one who is having fun interested for a while.  The areas are large and open (and this is not a linear game), the customization is one of the more unique things I've seen out of an RPG, and the character recruitment process is slightly unpolished, among other things in the game, but the idea of having so many optional characters with histories and personalities is a nice touch.  If the price is low enough (and this game can go pretty low, price-wise) then I'd definitely recommend checking it out, especially if your looking for a unique experience.

Hitman: Absolution is the fifth game in the long running Hitman series of video games. The game revolves around a so called "Agent 47" who works as an assassin for the Agency, a global contract killing society with enormous funding and resources.
This time, the game decides to break the usual formula of the series by being more focused on the story. In the previous titles you were usually assigned on a mission to kill a specific target by using a vast amount of different options available in the large-scaled sandboxy maps. In Absolution however, the levels are a lot more linear and focused around stealth 'em up style of gameplay. (Fans of Deus Ex: Human Revolution are probably familiar with this.) As a new player to the series, i dont personally think this as a bad thing since the story, graphics and voice acting are top notch and highly entertaining. I do understand however, how older fans of the series could find this a bit unsettling to say at least.
The gameplay in Hitman: Absolution is focused around you usually trying to kill a target with various different methods of your choice, this is the main seller of the game since you can experiment with the tools given to you in the levels and create some rather absurd scenarios. As i said though, this time the game does also have some linear levels where you are tasked to sneak past guards and escape buildings, it's not nearly as fun as the assassination missions but not bad either. The game rewards you by points for doing different tasks and ranks your score at the end of the level depending on how you performed. If you want to achieve the Silent Assassin rank you will need to be absolutely perfect with all your moves, this is not an easy task and will require a lot of replaying.
Like i said previously, the game is a super high budget AAA title. All the sound assets, textures, animations and so on are the absolute best the industry can offer you right now. Story elements in Absolution are handled by some in-game interaction and cutscenes that do the job surprisingly well. It's not anything groundbreaking but entertaining nonetheless.
In the end, Hitman: Absolution is a stellar title you shouldn't miss if you're a fan of stealth-action games and assassination. Just make sure you're not running a toaster since it's graphically a bit demanding.

Greetings Everyone!  My next stop was back to Torchlight a dungeon crawler that I feel tries to bring back that classic feeling of the original Diablo.  Overall it succeeds, for its time this was a great dungeon crawler for those wanting a classic feel with some cleaned up mechanics.  I still enjoyed my play through and is a great stepping stone towards Torchlight 2 (another game I highly recommend).
Stay awhile and Listen:  From the town to the indentify scrolls this game feels like the spiritual successor of Diablo and it is an enjoyable experience.  The story isn’t bad either albeit a bit bland (again not necessarily a bad thing for the game’s intent) and although I would have liked to see a bit more to do in the end I can’t complain as the core gameplay is so well done.  If you are trying to show someone classic dungeon crawl this is a better game to start with than some of the originals this game takes from.
Supersize me:  It cannot be understated how involved the mod community is for this game and how much it influences this game.  There is even an achievement for installing a mod and I find myself installing a mod almost immediately.  I know many of you won’t like this but I installed the respec potion mod.  I have never really understood the need for some to insist that choices like this have to be permanent.  Depending on the game it should be as easy as going to a town or as difficult as a month long process.  I just never feel a character (especially when the end game is good) should be permanently punished for a bad decision a new player made 5 minutes into playing.  I digress, give the mods out there a look; an argument could be made that you should probably play the game to completion before installing any to get the vanilla product down but it is your choice.
Ye Olde Classic:  Everything about this game screams classic dungeon crawl, even the difficulty if you decide to crank it up.  This is both to its credit and detriment as there are some issues that are caused by this design philosophy.  Some quality of life features are missing such as minion information:  I enjoy playing minion master type classes and it was hard for me to determine when I needed to respawn minions in the middle of massive battles.  The mini map could use a bit of work as it seems to take inspiration from older dungeon crawlers in this area too (TL2 massively improves upon this) and blends into the scenery.  Draw distance for enemies and even odd instances where enemies would phase in an out for odd reasons (no they weren’t teleporting).  Finally, some players may feel the game was too simple, with very basic leveling system and little to do other than the next level.  I can understand but do not agree with this.
So much of this game takes inspiration from Diablo and I love it, it was a great trek down memory lane.  But, is it worth buying now?  Simply put, yes.  There are some issues that much is obvious but the little issues are well worth the game itself.  If you are dungeon crawler who doesn’t have this game; get it.  It would also be a great buy to get someone into this genre.

About two weeks in, my group was desperately low on food and meds... Bruno wasn't looking too good, and Pavle had just been injured from a raid on my safehouse the night before... things were getting bad. Up to this point i had tried to be nice and not steal from people, only going to abandoned buildings and taking the things that nobody wanted... that wasn't an option anymore. Alright, i told myself, tonight you're going to have to steal something, but only what you need!
That night i set two people on guard while Pavle slept off his injury, Marko went out to scavenge. I arrive at my destination, a nice little townhouse in the middle of a warzone. I scavenge outside for a little bit and find some crafting material but what i really need is inside. I thought about my friends back at my safehouse and went in. Almost immediately Marko was caught. An elderly couple was sitting around a fire in their living room. The old man stood up and shouted fearfully at me to go away. I pulled out my knife and walked towards him, he backed down quickly and started begging for his and his wife's life. I didn't kill them, i walked right past him and went straight to their kitchen. He followed close behind me begging me not to take their things. They needed their food, they needed their meds... well i needed it more! I only took what i needed, but i wanted to make sure that i searched the house as fully as i could. I descended down the ladder into the basement and approached a locked door, i started prying it open with my crowbar. The old man, who was still following me begging me not to take his things, all of a sudden ran away. "Oh♥♥♥♥♥♥" i said to myself, "He's going to try and fight me." Before he got away in a moment of panic, i sprinted after him and stabbed him repeatedly... until he stopped moving. His wife called out to him, saw what i had done, and collapsed to her knees. I climbed up the ladder and stood over her. She called me a murderer... i didn't want to kill him, but my life, and the lives of my group, were more important than his. I searched the old man and took his things, looted the rest of the house... and ran to to exit...
Marko will remember this.

Crysis has definitely proven one of the best shooters of the past decade. It has become a personal favorite for me, as have the two sequels. However, the first installment of this series contains one element that the other two lack, namely a great amount of freedom. Much of the campaign covers large areas, with lots of space for you to manoeuver and outwit your enemies. This has been the most fun element in this game for me, playing it on the highest difficulty and letting it come down solely to the planning of your assault. In the parts of the game where you encounter the alien lifeforms, this element is taken away, and although graphically and story-wise they are a definite plus, this game is worth playing mainly because of the preceding part.
As for the graphics, not much needs to be said. This game runs along with recent installments of Battlefield and Call of Duty just fine. Gameplay-wise, it may even top those games. I strongly recommend it to anyone who likes shooters with some tactical elements and a more than decent science fiction story.

The biggest problem deserves the top slot: you can't do turn based multiplayer, you can't mod a multiplayer game.
The Civilization series is a solid pedigree that neatly defines an excellent rendition of a genre it practically defines.
Beyond Earth doesn't even try to live up to that reputation. The game fails to engage the player from the very beginning. Exploration is slow, growth is slower, research is even slower than that. I've only a few hours with this game but that's plenty to tell you where things have gone wrong.
The setting is bland. The world is a nameless place with bad graphics, the units are generic, and the factions have no personality, no historical connection. You can't watch Montezuma rant about Gandi and you can't listen to Morgan push his financial empire. There aren't factions, just teams with different colors.
The tech web is a joke. The jump in cost from one level to the next pretty much precludes any kind of directed research, unless you want to cripple your civilization that is.
The interface is...indescribably bad. Its poorly documented and does an equally poor job of documenting your empire. It's nearly impossible to keep track of where your explorers are and which teams you have decent relations with, let alone why you're researching a given tech.
The costs of every kind of action are so extreme that the game grinds to a halt. Don't expect to have an urban sprawl or really any kind of infrastructure. Exponential growth is cut short because even two workers will trip over eachother, leading to wasted time and resources.
Resource generation is specialized. No matter what you do, you're boned on all of it.
There's nothing this game does that Alpha Centauri or Civilization 4 didn't do better.

If you read the top reviews for this game, you'll notice the good review, but there is a GOOD reason for the low metascore. The amazing reviews ons team are most likely because the only people who will buy this game are already avid LOTR fans. I however, was not a fan beforehand and will deliver a serious review.
Here's a complied list, and at the end of the list I'll let you be the judge of whether or not you wish to dive into this game
Is the story any good?
Absolutely, as any RPG you have the freedom to partake in the story or to skip it and get into the action. Talking to the villagers of every town will get you side quests in which you can earn some intense gear.
Is the combat any good?
Personally, the combat is pretty repetetive, but it does allow for some customizing, much like dragon age.
Is there customization?
The customization is limited but it IS there, which is better than no customization. Note: You may only customize AFTER starting the game.
Diversity?
Yes, you're able to pick one of the three heros and go along with it, there's also multiplayer functions so you can bring two friends and each have their own hero.
All of these things are good, so why is this a downvote?
There is only one bad quality, but you must realize the depth of the how terrible it is to understand why it's a thumbs down.
What is wrong with it?
The game crashes OFTEN. This game was released on Nov. 1, 2011 which wasn't too long ago. Yet, the game runs like it was made in 2002, with how the graphics are I originally thought this game was made in 2006.
My computer is really new, and it is capable of running Bioshock infinite on max settings, yet it cannot run LOTR War in the North for over an hour without crashing. What's more, is that it does not simply crash the game/window/application. It crashes the ENTIRE DESKTOP.
THIS IS WHY THE GAME RECIEVED A LOW METASCORE, IT IS INCREDIBLY UNSTABLE. It is borderline unplayable, because up until the undead level, you don't really have any problems with crashing. but the second you get to the undead mobs, the game cannot control it's own software and seeminglye xplodes upon itself. And, because the undead levels are canon, you MUST pass through them. I was lucky because my computer was new, so I had a long grace period before it killed itself, but any run of the mill computer may not be able to handle it at all.
All in all, this was a great game, if it wasn't so cancerous to it's own programming, I as a person who is not a die-hard fan of LOTR can honestly say this would have recieved an 85-95 score for what it brings to the table. However, an amazing game CANNOT HAVE A FOUNDATION MADE SUITABLE ONLY FOR GAMES 5 YEARS BEHIND ITS TIME.

You play as a honey badger, and you have to take care of these 5 baby badgers and make sure you help them grow up. You are both a predator and somewhat of a prey, if you fail to watch out for the babies, one by one they all die. You could hunt foxes, frogs and etc, as well as eat fruits or vegatables and deliever them to your babies.

So you really have to depend on being stealthy if you're hunting foxes, but during my gameplay, they easily hear me when I'm a foot awat them and then they're off. The babies are basically useless and only drag you down. They will always follow you around which kinda gives your spot away when hunting for animals, and when bigger predators hunt you down. I once was trying to sleathly move across these grassy areas, and because of the babies being idiots, they slowly followed me and one big bird swooped right in and grabbed one.

It's basically a beautiful looking escort mission, and it's pretty annoying. I know there are people that are going to hate my review, but it's just how I feel about this game.

This is very much a game that you NEED (and I honestly mean that it is required) to read a how-to-play guide before you ever get started. Partly because the party/control/gameplay system is ridiculously convoluted at first, but also because there are inherently backwards gameplay things you absolutely need to know before you start.
For example, battle rank (BR). BR is basically determined by how many enemies you kill. It's not like EXP though, from what I understand, because (from what I've read) it more or less keeps track of the number of times you enter combat, and not anything related to the toughness of the monsters you kill. You want to keep BR as low as possible, since your characters get better stat increases at low BR, and the enemies will scale with you, potentially even causing you to be out-leveled at later stages in the game.
This is idiotic. Why the flaming crap do they fill areas chock-full of enemies that you can beat, and then say "Nuh-uh, you'll regret it later" and "You're doing the smart thing and attacking enemies one at a time!? HOW DARE YOU, NOW YOU MUST SUFFER!" Plus, this is not explained to you at all. Of course, neither is 98% of the rest of the game.
The combat is weird, and strangely hard to follow. You will assign your unions (squads of units) to attack certain other enemies, but when the attack round starts, the unions run at each other in this pre-scripted "action" scene that makes it really hard to mentally place where they are actually running to. It's hard to explain, but immediately noticeable. Honestly, this game would be way better if they cut out the cinematic crap and just gave you a flat overhead view of the battle.
Not a fan. I played it for maybe 10 hours, and was lost and frustrated for 10.6 of them. This game has no direction, no tutorials, and completely illogical gameplay mechanics. If you feel like studying guides for 5 hours before playing, be my guest. I choose to play something actually fun, and actually challenging without resorting to cheap tricks like withholding information.

If you loved the zany, crazy, madness that was Saints Row 4 - yes, thats including the superpowers and extremely insane themes. Then you will definitely get your money's worth with Gat Out of Hell.
Gat Out of Hell is short, but still very worth it for the price, especially if you are an SR4 fan. I would say that I hurried through the game, and with a time of about 6 hours 12 minutes, I finished the main story, all activities with gold and collected all collectables on Hardcore difficulty (97% game complete, plenty diversions and kill quests left to do, but those are just timesinks).  Of course this is quite short, but considering they marked the game down to 20 dollars (compared to 60 dollar releases of the same quality), I would still say its well worth the money, or at the very least on sale.
The story is.. a love-story!.. In hell! Without spoiling anything that isn't in the description of the game already, the President is kidnapped by Satan. He is to marry his daughter, Jezebel. And on top of that, the story is portrayed as a musical in a few instances. Additionally, regarding the story, if you are a fan of the story in the Saint's Row genre in general, you will find many references or even characters throughout the game that will make you either laugh or reminisce. The ending is one of various choices, that you get to choose yourself.
On top of the story we also have activites, as in previous Saint's Row games, these often tie into the story in a way that you have to finish them to progress, personally I find most of these fun, even in previous Saint's Row games, so I did not have much of a problem with them, but I know some people are less inclined to do them - or even to strive for gold.
They have added a dozen variations to previous activities, and a bunch that are based on the new flight power - such as "Salvation", you have to fly to falling souls and catch them before they reach the ground, without landing on the ground yourself.
Gameplay is very similar to Saint's Row 4, in the sense that a lot of the superpowers are very similar, if not the same - with a few exceptions, such as "Summon", an ability to summon, for instance, an army of imps! Yes, that's right, your very own army of imps that will jump and attach themselves to your enemies while gnawing at their heads/limbs.
As for bugs/glitches, I have yet to stumble across any - I did find a few activities that seemed like they could do with some tweaking in time, but to be frank, this might just be a matter of getting through the learning curve and optimizing how I do it better.
I encountered a single bug that made me only get 939/940 of the soul clusters needed, this was a little annoying. (Edit: Turns out it was simply not on the map, but it was ingame, I found it now and have 940/940, link to map in comments).
Saint's Row Insanity at its best.
New activities/variations of old activities. (Salvation, Torment Fraud, Hellblazing with flight)
New targets (Most are similar to SR4, but again, have a variation).
New Map (Uses the same city-theme as the others, with a hell twist - but it is a new map)
Characters from the older games (Dane, Dex, DeWynter sisters) + a few new original ones (Shakespeare, Vlad, etc).
Plenty of new awesome weapons (7 deadly sins).
New superpowers (Summon is entirely new, and all the others have new "Elements"/variations).
Story is as cheesy as any good Saint's Row story should be.
It's cheap. At $20 you still get much more content and usage than a movie ticket. (Now imagine the inevitable 75% off at $5).
Game is not reinventing itself. And while this is not THAT bad, because I am a huge fan of the SR series, it would be nice with some more variety from SR4.
It's short - took me 6 hours to beat the story, gold all activities, and find all collectibles - could probably have been done faster. Still worth the $20 pricemark though, and definitely 50%-75% off if you can wait.
Not enough Genki, although you do get to kill him at least once.
Not enough old characters - Why not let us fight more old baddies again, let Gat kill Jyunichi (Aisha's killer) some more? Or Killbane for that matter?
Not enough Shaundi and Pierce. Gat and Kinzie are great, sure, but couldn't they at least have had some more banter between them?
There was no gang-war at all in this one, again, sure it's hell and all but..
No radios - Who wouldn't have LOVED a hell-themed radio-set? Imagine talkshow hosts in hell, maybe even interviewing Satan?
As a Saint's Row fan I will be inclined to recommend this at its full price no problem, if you love the series and cant get enough of SR4 - then get this for sure. Otherwise, you might want to hold off until it's 50% off. It's still a great addition to the series, and I've had a lot of fun with it already - and will most definitely continue doing so.
After 14 hours and 51 minutes, I 100%'d the game - this could definitely have been done faster, but I wasn't exactly speed-rushing through it. Of course, this is excluding 1 achievement (Spend 20 hours in hell).

First let me say I played the iphone version alot before the pc version was released.
This game is decent.. MTG in its own right is great, but as far as this PC game version goes, it isnt better than magic 2015, maybe even worse, considering technical issues and DRM. Sure you can technicly play the game offline but you cant earn coins, which is the only way to buy new cards besides real money, and your progress in the campaign doesnt save.  So in other words if you get disconnected from their servers or your internet is down, there isnt much point in playing.
This would be alot better if/when they add more cards, add better offline play but also add more features that other games like Hearthstone or even MTGO already have. Some sort of tournament mode and/or Draft mode would really be great.
Yes two-headed giant is back, but it doesnt eaern coins or improve your rank so its only fun to play with a friend casually.
To me the "improved" deck builder is pretty much the same as the one in Magic 2015, its ok, but for anyone who knows anything about magic, its probably best to just customize your own deck, especially after aquiring more cards.
Also with this game being multiplatform, some cross save features would be nice so you dont have to unlock cards multiple times between platforms, especially if you spent real money on them.
I'd give this a 6/10 as it is, if you love MTG its worth giving a shot since it is free, but if you are just looking for a good Computer TCG, stick with something like Hearthstone.

I'm really enjoying Hollow knight! I like the way the story isnt beat over your head in the typical fantasy-sense ("You are the chosen one, you must save the world from evil!"). Hitman…. The game where the only problem with the game is my skill.
Hitman Absolution in my opinion an amazing game, graphic wise and gameplay wise.
– Storyline 8/10
As much a fan as I am of the game, the storymode could have been worked on just a little more! I found it confusing to what’s happening from time to time. Sometimes I didn’t even know if there was a story mode. The story mode starts with you assassinated Diana. Your assignment is to kill Diana and bring Victoria a teenage girl who you find out later is quite special. The game becomes more interesting when you decide to hide Victoria in a nearby church therefore disobeying the Agency’s order.
– Controls 7/10
Controls of the game weren’t too bad, but were a bit wonky at times. I didn’t particularly like the idea of QTE’s for every close combat battle you get into though.
– A.I. 8/10
The A.I. was just spot on, untill they started hiding behind walls and shooting through them. I also had problems with the fact that everyone knows EVERYONE, I was no more special then the next guy, but apparently I stand out in a crowd. Also sometimes the A.I. somehow know where you are when trying to throw an item to distract them.
– Graphics 10/10
I honestly can’t complain about the graphics, I didn’t find any bugs or glitches in the particles around me. I also didn’t notice texture poping or not rendering. There are plenty of options for the resolution of the game for those who own a less powerful computer.
– Options 10/10
The options menu in a lot of games is quite poorly done, but in Hitman Absolution it was executed perfectly. You can change every control, the difficulty of the game, graphics and more.
– Gameplay 10/10
Obviously the main part of the game, executed perfectly. Hitman Absolution has 2 gamemodes to choose from – Storymode & Contracts. The story mode explains itself. The contracts can add a few more hours after finishing story mode. In the Contracts mode you compete against friends and online players to who can be the best assassin. Little side note- If you fail any level in storymode or contracts it has a really quick and easy replayabilty. The Chaoters are split into multiple levels, which alows the levels to be designed better and makes it easier to replay if necessary. One of my most beloved aspects of the game is – you can finish a level or choose a path in more than 1 ways. Often you will be given the choice to garote a victim or smash his head in with a vase you just picked up a minute ago.
– Final Verdict 8/10
The game in my opinion is amazing. I have nothing to add. Buy it. Play it. Enjoy it.

I own the hard copy of this game, though it doesn't seem to work well anymore, but I still have put at least 300 hours into the game, I've had it for a long time and it was pretty much my childhood.
The game in a nutshell is an ARPG lootfest with three "Classes" to choose from, The Alchemist, The Destroyer, and the Vanquisher. The Alchemist is pretty much the mage class, and great for summoning minions. The Destroyer is a figher, and the Vanquisher is more or less the rogue/ranger class.
However, in the game, any class can use any weapon, provided they meet the minimum criteria. So this game allows any player to play how they want to, wanna use firearms? pick up a pair and start blasting. Swords? Shields? Dual wield? Go for it. LIke them mad DPS? like the big numbers? They got weapons for that too!
Personally, I found The Alchemist to be the most useful, because he has a lot of spells that are great crowd control. Trust me, crowd control is a MUST in this game, as you will often start hacking and slashing away at many enemies at once on screen, so its possible to get lost in the chaos. The Alchemist also has Minion spells, which come in handy, as your pet can only handle so many enemies at once. I believe he can summon up to six Nether imps(on a maxed out skill) a steam golem, a beam golem, and possibly one other construct of some sort, all at the same time, so you have eight minions, your pet and yourself, to tackle an end game dungeon, which WILL come in handy as the Dragon dungeon will be INCREADIBLY HARD!
The story is You coming to Torchlight for...(insert character's reason's here) only to find out that there is this rogue master, or something along that lines, and you end up getting corrupted by the same thing he is, and you have to set out to cure it. From there its a bit fuzzy as I can remember only so much, but this game overall, is worth it.
The voice acting isn't bad either, granted most of the voice acting is narration, but it still doesn't ruin the immersion.
Overall I would give this game a 7/10 as there are a couple things they need to improve on such as a little lesh restrictive character choice, more pets, and enemies.
I would still recommend you buy it, and play it for yourself, because this game can easily steal 30 hours of your life away.

In this game you play a gamer who is working for a company called Abstergo. There you are playing a game about Pirates and your actions and footage are captured. All the while you are covertly researching the company you are working for.
Black Flag is easily the 2nd or third best AC game I've played so far and arguably one of the finest Piracy games around.
The game really reaches its climax once you have upgraded the Jack Daw, but the real, sad finale is walking around Abstergo  looking for post it notes and hacking computers. I know right?
The main negatives:
* Ship boarding becomes repetitive and dull.  It should only be necessary for ships with larger crews, smaller ships should automatically lay down their weapons.
* Shanty chasing
* Abstergo sequences and collection is dull and oddly they are first person.
Surprises:
Unexpectedly I was delighted by some of the dreamier sequences in the game. I don't expect such things in open world titles, but to drive home the emotional impact of the events on a character they are a delightful way of doing it.
The iOS app helps to deal with the otherwise super repetitive cash grind game. But the final destinations have returns times that are more than a day. To be honest I had not unlocked all destinations before finishing the game and had to keep playing the app for a week to get one more lousy Abstergo achievement.

I've never rage quit an AC game for progression reasons before, but I did with that.
Aveline, on the other hand is easily within the top 3 AC games. I was kinda hoping this would be the same with Freedom Cry. I'm sure there is a good game in there, but I'm not going back to it for a while.

About two weeks in, my group was desperately low on food and meds... Bruno wasn't looking too good, and Pavle had just been injured from a raid on my safehouse the night before... things were getting bad. Up to this point i had tried to be nice and not steal from people, only going to abandoned buildings and taking the things that nobody wanted... that wasn't an option anymore. Alright, i told myself, tonight you're going to have to steal something, but only what you need!
That night i set two people on guard while Pavle slept off his injury, Marko went out to scavenge. I arrive at my destination, a nice little townhouse in the middle of a warzone. I scavenge outside for a little bit and find some crafting material but what i really need is inside. I thought about my friends back at my safehouse and went in. Almost immediately Marko was caught. An elderly couple was sitting around a fire in their living room. The old man stood up and shouted fearfully at me to go away. I pulled out my knife and walked towards him, he backed down quickly and started begging for his and his wife's life. I didn't kill them, i walked right past him and went straight to their kitchen. He followed close behind me begging me not to take their things. They needed their food, they needed their meds... well i needed it more! I only took what i needed, but i wanted to make sure that i searched the house as fully as i could. I descended down the ladder into the basement and approached a locked door, i started prying it open with my crowbar. The old man, who was still following me begging me not to take his things, all of a sudden ran away. "Oh♥♥♥♥♥♥" i said to myself, "He's going to try and fight me." Before he got away in a moment of panic, i sprinted after him and stabbed him repeatedly... until he stopped moving. His wife called out to him, saw what i had done, and collapsed to her knees. I climbed up the ladder and stood over her. She called me a murderer... i didn't want to kill him, but my life, and the lives of my group, were more important than his. I searched the old man and took his things, looted the rest of the house... and ran to to exit...
Marko will remember this.

Pros: Story, Graphics, Sounds
Cons: Controls, Value
Magic Duels: Origins takes players through the lives of the five most iconic characters in Magic.  The gameplay and story weave nicely together to create an interesting and exciting campaign.  The graphics and sounds are mostly great: not much artistic or technical prowess is needed for a digital card game, but the few cutscenes definitely could have been more polished.
Controls work well enough, but some elements of the game's earlier mobile design leak through.  For example, many gameplay controls are placed in the lower righthand corner where a quick thumbpress is perfect for some hardware, but rather clumsy for others.
However, the biggest problem with Magic Duels: Origins lies in its value.  While certainly worth playing for the story, Magic Duels has so little worth beyond its campaign.  Every card could be collected given enough time, but in-game transactions speed the process tremendously.  Why spend the money?  To reach the top rank of this year's beginner program? The money would be better off spent on Magic: the Gathering Online or on the actual cardboard.

Very fun and enjoyable game overall. Also extremely well polished, especially considering the price it's going for right now. Amazing value for money. I generally look for a game that I can pick up and play on the run, quickly, since I often dont have that much time. This does the job perfectly. I can play it for as long as I need, or just pick it up for a few minutes, play a skirmish, and work on my items.
The highlight of the game and where it shines I would say is the multiplayer, and the ease of carrying out combat. Very good replay value, with trying to get better and better items. I really like that you don't have to focus on gathering resources. Your entire focus is on your army, what the enemy has, and how to best counteract their troops. In some ways it's like a flashy game of chess, but on a much more dynamic level.
The only downside right now is that the community is still small. The more players get into it the better. I'd give it overall a 9.5/10. It sets out to achieve a specifc task, and does so perfectly. And again...I can't believe the price for such a polished overall product. Excellent.

War in the North is a fairly boring action rpg.  The story of the game is that your party, that consists of a ranger, elf, and dwarf, is on a journey to stop another evil baddie other than Sauron.  This journey takes place as Frodo and the fellowship are on their way to destroy the ring.  Because of this setting, you can feel the B-side nature of it.  You do see some of the fellowship in Rivendell but the conversations boil down to, "Hey buddy, I'm doing this.  What are you doing?"  Oh yeah, they are talking eagles in this game.  TALKING EAGLES.
Gameplay is a bit drab.  While I do enjoy the brawler genre, this game borders on Dynasty Warriors mindless and straight up boredom.  You have two main attacks, one standard and one strong.  You also have skills which are accessed through modifier triggers.  While useful, having those abilities limited by both a cooldown and power bar restricts you from using them all the time and only when it matters.  I had about 30 power potions left when I finished the game mainly due to me using them sparingly.  You have a block but it's useless.  It's hard to tell whether your character will actually block or take damage.  The only satisfying thing about the combat is that you get to decaptitate foes or sever their limbs for extra experience.
Unless you are a LOTR nut, stay away.

I've played every Civ, ever. Bottom line: This one sucks. It goes out of its way to be a new twist on the old formula, and it succeeds only in being cumbersome and annoying. Cases in point:
a. It's completely linear, and boringly so. The only way to win (unles you restrict winning to Domination only) is to proceed directly toward a particular type of victory. It leaves absolutely no margin to deviate from a linear path to victory. In other words, if you don't go directly after one particular type of victory from the very start of a game, you will lose very quickly.
b. Despite being completely linear, it uses a tech web to make itself look less linear than the old tech trees, but all this does is increase the learning curve, given that the only way to win is to directly pursue a particular style of victory.
c. It has an almost complete lack of functionality and lack of everything. Forget awesome stuff like random great people, or wonders that do game-changing stuff. The vast majority of technologies simply increase your total output of energy, culture, etc... But they do very little that's exciting. Since it's totally linear, you're highly restricted in the types of units you can build. And if you want to improve the units you've built, you have to research very particular technologies. Of course, easier technologies are researched faster and, thus, earlier in the game. So, again, it's completely linear, and very boring.
I'm hopeful that some expansions will fix the numerous shortcomings with this game. But, as it is now, it completely fails to live up to the standards of the Civilization franchise. In sum: It's a bust, and you shouldn't buy it.

For me, my definitive space sim is "Descent Freespace: The Great War", because it was the first to not only captivate me by story, but also it's, then, fluid controls, independent and "sentient-like" AI, and excellent characterizations.  Since then, most space sims I've tried have pailed significantly...until, now.  For me, this is still not quite "Descent" but it's by far been the most engaging I've played recently in the genre.  A lot of its gameplay and story points are nothing new (though very well executed), but it's main selling point, imo, comes in (similar to "Descent") the grand space battles with independent NPCs...and that's what I love!  You aren't some omnipotent Space Ace, but one cog in a slowly dying army trying to survive.  All of your allied ships from your wingmen to the grand capitol ships cause damage on the enemy...and once you get past the first few missions, there's A LOT of you in the quadrant.  Not only are you dodging that Colonial fighter chasing your tail...but also the stray shots coming from other dogfights in surrounding you.  This is truly the closest, today, that one can come to feeling what Robotech/Macross, Star Wars, Star Trek, Wing Commander, etc. Space battles were like.

War in the North was that one game that I had heard nothing but mediocre things about. "The AI is terrible," whined every reviewer, "and the story is complete garbage, not to mention the clunky gameplay." With words like these clouding my vision, my buddy and I decided to give it a whirl one day out of sheer boredom. Maybe it was my initially abysmal expectations, but I was thoroughly satisfied, and in some cases, completely blown away.
Now, that's not to say that the reviewers were lying. The story is extremely silly, but that's not really the focus of the game. It only took us about an hour to realize that this is in no way a story-driven game. It's a pure hack-and-slash at it's finest, the likes of which I've never seen before. In this area, the game outshines just about every other RPG out there.
This is one of the most fun action games there is... provided you have friends to play with, because the reviewers weren't kidding when they said the AI is absolutely awful. For instance, if you happen to get knocked down in combat, your the AI will focus 100% on making his way to save you. Great, right? Except for that massive troll about to wail on him with a giant hammer. We had very few kind words for our AI friend.
The RPG elements are pretty simple, but again, that's because the focus is right where it should be: the combat. The difficulty spikes in satisfying ways, lulling you into complacency, then smacking you in the face with a horde of Uruk-hai.
Beyond the standard gameplay, there are little touches here and there that make this game worthwhile. For one example, the in-game voice chat adds an echo effect to your voice when you enter a cave. Pretty neato, right? It's features like that, which, while being completely unnecessary to the core experience, add a sense of joy to the playing experience, and brought a smile to my face.
In summary, if you have a friend or two to play with, and you're looking for a decent-length hack-and-slash with light RPG elements, this is the game for you.

Having been looking forward to this for a while, I finally bought it (on sale).  Despite the complaints, it really isn't so bad.
It does feel like an initial CIV version release.  In that the AI is weakish and totally insane.  The learning curve is rocky and steep, you can't play this like you've been playing historical civ.  However, once you figure it out, it feels comfortable.
There are complaints about the ease of the AI.  It does seem to be simplistic in its heuristics.  It also is very insane as I noted above.  I had one declare war on me with no excuses in the diplomacy window.  They didn't last long and quit the war in a few turns, but all the while they were still trading with me with their convoys.
In addition, when building and using the end game object, the AI doesn't seem to care.  Granted, I am sure to build a sufficient military to fend off anyone who might come along, but it never happens.  They only attack if your military level falls below a certain level.  This you find out when you do the ending where you send your armies through the gate.  Since your military score is going down, you will have a neighbor declare war (after all, its only business).
Still the game in general isn't bad.  If Firaxis follows the same pattern they have been with the other Civ games, it will be quite good in a few expansions.  It isn't terrible now.
So, I give this a thumbs up.
NOTE: If you are getting and playing this game hoping it is a modern Alpha Centauri. It isn't.  There isn't nearly the depth of strategy here.  No terraforming, no unit design decisions, no back story of the planet unfolding as you struggle to live on and learn about this planet.  Once you get passed that, you'll be more comfortable with it.

This game is absolutely astounding! Constant updating, developers know what they're doing, and great fun. If you've ever played smash bros., You'll like it. If you've enjoyed competitive Melee, you'll love it. If you've enjoyed competitive melee but felt all the hidden tech and exhausting inputs were scary or would take too long to master, you'll adore it and sacrifice Brawl discs in its name. Even if you've never played a smash-style fighting game, this is a great way to start.
Pros
easy on the eye graphics
incredibly responsive controller support
All the things you loved from smash, with the "bad" things removed and replaced with even better things
a competitive game that is still friendly to newcomers and casuals while helping and appreciating the veterans and devoted
compotent online systems and interface
characters are carefully optimized and constructed for balanced, unique, and riveting gameplay
new mechanics for smash veterans to adapt to, while still being familiar
characters combine classic characters from smash while introducing new "Gimmicks" that change the way you play entirely
You can play online or with friends. Local play with friends turns into a ritualistic pastime. Playing online helps you gauge how good you are, and there's always practice mode to figure out confirms and interesting tricks. Don't be afraid to buy this if you can't play with others locally, practice with the coms till you have a good grasp (don't forget the tutorial that is equally informative to complete newcomers and Melee gods), then go online and test yourself.
A new base game that will have you discovering new things well after 100 hours
Dan Fornace is very active in the community and is responsive to criticism and, as mentioned, applies input into frequent updates
cool "Make your own outfit" option I never saw coming
After playing through the turorials and getting a hang on how the game works, hidden tech and mechanics come very organically and a frame display in practice mode will teach you anything you didn't learn otherwise.
Awesome music (especially the airships)
great stages with a sort of "Omega" switch that makes them more tourney-legal, and base stages with fun and wacky active factors.
Cons
Graphics can be described as simplistic and certain frames during animations can look pretty wierd
due to the scrutiny of each character, there are only 8
because it's this type of game, regular keyboard controls are probably foreign and confusing (Although I've only used keyboard maybe once or twice, so I'm not even sure on that)
Although it is much better than earlier versions, there is still just enough lag in some matches that can trip up your inputs and cost you the game, but still better than sm4sh's average online experience.
Some say the game can be a bit scary to newcomers and is really meant for smash players looking for a new game or migratory melee players. I don't believe so myself, but I've been playing smash my whole life so I may have a bias.

Didn’t have enough space for my full review, so here’s a shortened version.

I will try tagging anything that may be a spoiler, as well as try to let you know what to expect.


You begin by attempting to rescue the main character's sister from the hands of a military organization while they "purge" on civilians. So you immediately see the opposing force and get a feeling for how big and violent they are. After doing the rescuing bit, you then proceed to flee from the military force for a long time. In fact, you flee from the military without a real antagonist until around chapter
Mix that with the challenging fate/destiny and the main goal may not always be so clear. By the time your group decides what they want to do, the game is almost over... Obviously, that is not everything that happens, but rather a grossly simplified version that they adhere to while other story events happen; such as being arrested, rescue missions, invading cities, etc.

The game presents itself by being very cutscene heavy and most the current storytelling and character development is done this way. Cutscenes are in predictable locations and the combat does not open up until chapter
, so some will probably see this as just travelling from one cutscene to another. This chapter changes the entire game by becoming very open with little cutscenes and lasts the longest. Afterwards, it goes back to the other formula for the rest of the game.
If you have some kind of aversion to cutscenes, there exists an option within the in-game menu called the "Datalog". This holds pretty much everything you could ever want to know. You can find summaries of the story here, character profiles, historical records and even the bestiary. Because this holds so much knowledge, if you're not too keen on reading these datalog entries, some events may seem random or confusing. Reading the datalog is completely optional and the game gives you some key points about the history within cutscenes.



There are 6 roles: Commando(the big physical damage dealer), Ravager(the chain gauge builder), Saboteur(the debuffer), Synergist(the buffer), Medic(the healer), Sentinel(the tank). You eventually unlock all roles. These roles allow you to create multiple combinations with the characters that you can and will change through a lot during battle. However, the game does not fully open up each role’s mechanics until about 19-20 hours into the game and that is a pretty long time.
You have 3 characters at maximum on the battlefield at once, while only ever directly controlling one. And you'll be mostly using an Auto Battle option that does exactly as the name implies. Auto Battle chooses the most helpful attack at that moment and can often lead to you just mashing the button until the enemy dies. This will not work for every fight, but you can complete the storyline with a little bit of grinding using mainly Auto Battle. However, you cannot expect to easily defeat post-game enemies this way. Launch is a skill that is learned later, which launches an enemy in the air if their staggered bar is filled. Thus, an optimal strategy is to try and juggle launched enemies since they cannot attack unless standing on the ground.


If you lose a fight, the game puts you right before that fight and you try again.
When a fight ends, you fully heal all of your HP making the battles much more offensive based. This makes sense as there is no resource management like MP in the game and in battle, you can use any skill as long as you have the required number of ATB sections filled.
The leveling up is extremely linear. You just choose which role you want your person to master and then throw your experience into it. You can prioritize some over others, but you'll eventually fill everything up to the max if you plan on doing post-game. Also, another welcome change is EXP is shared through everyone whether they are in your party or not! This lets you run around with your favorite characters and not have to worry about evening out the experience.



The game has very linear, narrow hallways for the majority of the game. The same chapter that changes everything introduces you to a giant field filled with creatures and treasure. Among the vastness of this expansive landscape, there exists "NPCs" that tell you a short story in written text and then order you to go kill something. There are numerous of these missions and they always require you to kill something. In addition, you can only do around half or so of these until post-game.
Enemies are seen while walking around instead of random battles, so you can avoid a lot of fights by sneaking around their line of sight despite being in a close corridor. The enemies also have a very distinct aggro zone.






Most everything feels appropriate and crisp when playing. From the ambient sounds of the jungle to listening to a robotic armadillo dig tunnels in the distance, it all sounds in place and sets the tone nicely. However, the footsteps could definitely use more variety. While they do make different sounds depending on ground you tread, they will always make those very similar two footstep sounds any time you step on the same material. This becomes far more apparent when travelling on metal and you have to hear the same clanks over and over again.

Fantastic musical score. This soundtrack includes serene and peaceful piano ballads, intense and heart-pumping orchestral pieces, and even strange ambient tracks meant to incite unease. I seriously cannot tell you how great this soundtrack is.

The game offers both English and Japanese audio so what's not to like? The English version was very well done and I prefer it over the Japanese.


This game definitely is not for everyone, especially if you think Final Fantasy 7 is the best because you played it when you were a child. I personally think this is one of the greatest entries in the entire series. As strange as it sounds, this game gives me a very strong, calming, and pure blissful feeling when I play it. This is the second time I hit 100% in this game, with the first being on Xbox 360. When asked why I love this game so much, I immediately think of the stunning visuals, outstanding sound track and memorable characters. However, Hope is dead to me. When you pair misguided anger with a child, you have two of the most abhorrent characteristics coming together resulting in the worst character in Final Fantasy history and I wish they just killed him off. While this game may lack certain story aspects and straightforwardness that is usually found in Final Fantasy games, I enjoyed what was presented. Far too many people criticize this game on what it's not instead of looking at what it did right. I agree that Final Fantasy XIII could be better and there are issues with it, but I enjoyed the game's successes far more than the negatives. Whether this will help someone decide if they want to try it, I do not know... but I suppose this was just my way to help me understand why I liked the game.
If you can look past the negatives and want to dive into the game and experience it for what it offers, you will not be disappointed. Whether you have played other Final Fantasy games or not, this game is accessible to anyone. However, if you're looking for a game to just check off a list and you lack patience, it would most likely be best for everyone if you decide to pass on this installment (and the other two XIII games) of the Final Fantasy series.
